sentences.text: Staphylococcus epidermidis is a coagulase-negative bacterium and a normal member of the human skin microbiota, with high strain-level diversity between people.
On skin it is not a passive resident: it primes the cutaneous immune response, helps maintain homeostasis and blocks opportunistic pathogens through colonisation resistance.
It is also a nasal commensal whose abundance rises before adulthood as pathogenic bacteria decline, an effect partly reversed in seniors, and it stimulates epithelial antimicrobial peptides.

A review describes it as the most common cause of implant-associated infections whose pathogenicity is attributed mainly to biofilms on indwelling devices, while another review says it apparently evolved not to cause disease.

references.title: Staphylococcus epidermidis and its dual lifestyle in skin health and infection.
